title: Risk Notebook: concise audit trail and guardrail composer for batching & cache decisions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers and operators configuring Redwood caching/batching policies need a compact, explainable audit trail that surfaces why recommendations were suggested, the risk profile of each setting, and an easy way to compose rollback/mitigation recipes. Existing UX patterns (large playbooks and modal forms) are too heavyweight for fast ops decisions during rollouts.

Goal: Prototype a lightweight 'Risk Notebook' pane in the Console that provides: an append-only timeline of configuration diffs; an inline risk score with short rationale for each change; quick buttons to compose guardrail actions (e.g., scale down batch size, enable prefix cache only, set canary traffic); and exportable snapshots for runbooks and compliance logs. The Notebook should be readable in a single glance on a 1366px width dashboard column and support comment annotations by SRE/PM/Design.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates the Notebook anchored to the Route details page displaying the last 5 config changes as compact cards
Each change card includes: author, time, diff summary (tokens/batch/kv-prefetch toggles), automated risk score (low/med/high) and a one-line rationale
Users can open a card to view a compact diff viewer (old vs new) with highlighted token-economy impact estimates
Quick action menu on each card with prefilled guardrail recipes (Canary 10%, Reduce batch by 25%, Enable prefix-only cache) that produce a follow-up config draft
Notebook supports adding short comments (<=280 chars) and marks which comments are actioned
Design handoff files (Figma + redlines) and a minimal accessibility checklist are delivered
PM/Eng signoff that the UI fits within the Console's 3-column layout and can be implemented without breaking existing rollout pipeline APIs
decisions: Use a compact card list instead of a full-screen timeline to reduce cognitive load
Risk score will be computed client-side from normalized telemetry signals (latency delta, token cost delta, error rate) and annotated with the top 2 contributing signals
Guardrail recipes are templates that map to existing rollout APIs; UI produces a prefilled draft request rather than firing changes directly
Comment model will be simple (flat, no threading) to keep implementation minimal for MVP
